Recommend adding it to the exclusion list, or treating platform-internal schemas as expected-absent-on-target; not a copy defect. classification.finding: 27x constraint_missing_in_a, all contype='n' (NOT NULL), one per not-null column across all 4 tables
classification.explanation: PostgreSQL 17+ (target is 18.6) materializes column NOT NULL as named, catalogued pg_constraint rows (contype='n'); PostgreSQL 16 (source) does not catalogue them as constraint objects, only as pg_attribute.attnotnull. Independently re-confirmed this round: fresh inventory snapshots on both sides show identical `nullable: false` on every affected column on BOTH source and target (e.g. blog_posts.slug, .title, .id, etc.). No column changed nullability; this is a version-inherent catalog representation difference, not a schema regression. schema-diff.mjs's exclusion list still does not ignore contype='n' entries the way it ignores owner/ACL/comments; recommend adding that exclusion given the target-PG-major-bump decision (A1 C2). Unchanged from round 1.
